numerical_failure.observed_behavior: Local-to-UTC shift of a Timestamp near the int64 bound wraps silently: with zoneinfo timezone, ts.tz_localize('America/New_York') raises ValueError saying the time is a nonexistent DST time, and with nonexistent='NaT' returns NaT; with use_tzlocal/fixed-offset timezones, two or more values near Timestamp.min/max come back in year -2262 (int64 wraparound).
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: An unrepresentable UTC result should raise OutOfBoundsDatetime (e.g. 'Converting ... overflows past 2262-04-11 23:47:16.854775807') instead of wrapping int64 or returning the NaT sentinel.
trigger_conditions: Timestamp whose wall time shifted to UTC lands outside int64 range, e.g. pd.Timestamp('2262-04-11 21:47:16.854775807') localized to America/New_York
zoneinfo fallback path in _get_utc_bounds where candidate UTC instant is computed by bare subtraction
use_tzlocal or fixed-offset timezone with two or more values near Timestamp.min/max
shift landing exactly on the NaT sentinel (one below minimum representable value)

input_output_examples.buggy_output: ValueError: ... is a nonexistent time due to daylight savings time

oracle_clues: Reproducer assertions: ValueError/NaT before fix, OutOfBoundsDatetime after fix
Commit states two or more values near Timestamp.min/max in fixed-offset or tzlocal zone came back in year -2262
Timestamp.tz_localize now raises OutOfBoundsDatetime when value == NPY_NAT and ambiguous/nonexistent not 'NaT' (GH#66550)

numerical_characteristics.precision: nanosecond (ns) resolution; datetime64[ns] values stored as int64 with NPY_NAT sentinel
numerical_characteristics.magnitude: values near Timestamp.min/max (int64 bounds, e.g. 2262-04-11 21:47:16.854775807 and Timestamp.max._value minus 2 hours)
category_specific_evidence: Bug is int64 wraparound in tz_localize_to_utc: a bare subtraction val - delta wraps past int64 bounds, producing a value in year -2262 instead of raising OutOfBoundsDatetime (commit message, test_tz_localize_overflow_fixed_offset).

Round-trip check in _get_utc_bounds fails for a wrapped candidate, leaving both bounds NaT; caller reports 'nonexistent time due to daylight savings time' or silently returns NaT under nonexistent='NaT' (diff tzconversion.pyx:621-654, commit message).

Reproducer: pd.Timestamp('2262-04-11 21:47:16.854775807').tz_localize('America/New_York') should raise OutOfBoundsDatetime ('overflows past 2262-04-11 23:47:16.854775807'); with nonexistent='NaT' it should raise rather than return NaT (PR#66698 reproducer).

Sentinel case: a shift landing exactly on NaT sentinel (-(2**63) + 9*3600*10**9 as M8[ns]) is one below minimum representable value and must raise OutOfBoundsDatetime with 'underflows past' (GH#66550 test).
Fixed-offset overflow test requires at least 2 values; length-1 DatetimeIndex boxes the lone value and masks the overflow downstream (test_tz_localize.py).

Past-last-cached-transition test: DatetimeIndex([Timestamp(Timestamp.max._value - 2*3600*10**9)]).tz_localize('America/New_York') with kwargs {}, nonexistent='NaT', or 'shift_forward' should raise OutOfBoundsDatetime matching 'overflows past'.
Fix in diff at tzconversion.pyx:357-365 wraps shift with _shift_to_utc and raises raise_out_of_bounds(v, BS_UNDERFLOW) when result equals NPY_NAT.
reproduction_risks: Length-1 DatetimeIndex masks the fixed-offset overflow; reproduction must use at least two values.
Timezone-dependent: the wrap for the reproducer depends on America/New_York and the April EDT offset; other zones or offsets may not overflow identically.
Expected behaviour before the fix (ValueError vs silent NaT) differs by nonexistent argument; reproduction must check the kwarg used.
